DIGITAL DISINFORMATION

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How vulnerable are we to digital propaganda and misinformation? We reveal how digital misinformation is being used to manipulate ordinary South Africans

Unique Selling Point:
We look at the sinister motives of digital disinformation through several compelling case studies

1. We look at how afrophobic and xenophobic sentiment was spread on social media by the fake "Lerato Pillay" twitter account. We look at the weaponizing of the #putsouthafricansfirst hashtag through the work of the DFR Lab - who unearthed and exposed the true identity of the Lerato Pillay

2. Similarly we look at the fake Tracey Zille twitter account. A South African government official posing as a racist white woman on Twitter posted several racially incendiary tweets that were designed to spark outrage. The furor generated by these tweets was used to funnel users to at least three of his websites, where he hoped to net an income off the back of the outrage caused by his tweets.

3. Finally, A network of racially charged websites used narratives of white victimhood in South Africa to turn a profit. The website domains are owned by a South African company called CoZaNic, operated by a man named Deon Venter.

Summary:
Digital disinformation and propaganda is becoming an increasing problem all over the world. We've seen how disinformation campaigns have been used to affect the outcome of the Brexit referendum and the 2016 US presidential election. Closer to home, we've seen the damage wrought by the white monopoly capital/ radical economic transformation campaign of PR firm Bell Pottinger

Over the past 4 years, the problem has only gotten worse with more sophisticated and insidious campaigns being launched against an unsuspecting public. We've seen the rise of Q-Anon in America while here in South Africa, xenophobic and overtly racist sentiment is being used to target ordinary South Africans. The #PutSoutAfricansFirst hashtag has been weaponised and used to disseminate vile afrophobic propaganda that could possibly incite real world violence.

In this story we reveal several of disinformation campaigns and how they were uncovered through the world of the Digital Forensic Research lab, an organization based in Cape Town who are a part of international think-tank The Atlantic Council

We'll visit their lab in the the Mother City to see the forensic techniques they employed to reveal the true perpetrators of these digital campaigns. We'll see the technology they have at their disposal and how it is used to join the dots and unmask the real culprits behind these fake news campaigns

We'll also speak with EFF MP Naledi Chirwa who was attacked by one of these digital campaigns with fake posts that threatened to expose her alleged fraudulent citizenship

We'll also speak with William Bird from Media Monitoring Africa. They've launched a campaign called the Real411, which provides a platform for members of the public to report disinformation and gain his insights into how prevalent the problem is in South Africa.

Finally we provide solutions to the problem: What can be done to stop disinformation campaigns?

Further information:
As the DFR lab are based in Cape Town, I am requesting that we fly to Cape Town to see their lab. One of the big beats in this story is the show and tell of how they've been able to identify disinformation campaigns. I want our presenter to experience this first hand and don't think we'd be able to achieve this through zoom intreviews

Press Release:


In a high-stakes virtual life where fresh news and new “likes” can mean power and income, the spreading of vital information that sparks emotion and harnesses a following, could be a powerful tool for good. But what if digital manipulation goes over to the dark side and targeted online campaigns bring about real-world hatred, conflict, confusion and harm? Carte Blanche investigates who and what lie behind misdirected hashtags on South African social media, intended to manipulate and exploit users. We analyse disinformation trends and meet the investigators who are unpacking fakes to help identify and combat the damage.
Producer: Julian Sun | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:









DIGITAL DISINFORMATION
Item Time GRAPHIC & VISUALS SCRIPT
1 30” INTRO SETTING UP A DIGITAL AGE OF DISINFORMATION


V/O: The world today is awash with disinformation or fake news, amplified by the algorithms of social media.

Anti-vaxxers, 5G towers that cause COVID-19 and Q-Anon are just some of the wild conspiracy theories gaining traction.

Even now, 2 weeks after the US election, President Donald Trump continues to insist (without any evidence) that the election was stolen from him. Twitter has flagged some of his tweets, disputing their veracity

LINK: These disinformation campaigns are becoming more sophisticated and coordinated and no country is immune, including South Africa…


2. 1’00 WHAT IS DISINFORMATION? The Atlantic Council’s Digital Forensic Research Lab specialises in exposing falsehoods and fake news. Jean Le Roux works for them.
1. What is disinformation?
2. What is the difference between disinformation and misinformation?

The Centre for Analytics and Behavioural Change is a non-profit organization dedicated exposing fake narratives online. Stuart Jones explains how big the problem is worldwide.

3. How big a problem is it worldwide and in South Africa?
3. 90” THE #PUTSOUTHAFRICANSFIRST HASHTAG








V/O: Working independently from one another, the DFR Lab and the CABC have exposed the biggest disinformation campaign in South Africa this year.

Since it first appeared in April, #PutSouthAfricansFirst has become the second most popular hashtag on South African twitter. It has been used in 393,000 tweets and generated more than a billion impressions so far. The DFR Lab’s Tessa Knight explains what’s so sinister about it.

Tessa Explains why they started investigating it

4. 60” UNEARTHING ULERATOPILLAY

V/O: One of the biggest drivers of the campaign was a fake twitter account going by the pseudonym “uLerato Pillay”

1. Explaining what the Lerato Pillay account was doing
2. We must go through when the account was set up and how it was able to amass tens of thousands of followers in few short months
3. The type of xenophobic, anti-immigrant tweets it was putting out
5. 90” SHOW AND TELL OF HOW DFR LAB WERE ABLE TO EXPOSE THE TRUE IDENTITY OF ULERATO PILLAY
1. A show and tell of how DFR did their work
2. Revealing the identity of Sifiso Gwala

V/O: We reached out to Sifiso Gwala via whatsapp and email but he did not respond to our requests for an interview

6. 60” WHO’S BEHIND THE PSAF HASHTAG?
V/O: The CABC & the DFR Lab believe uLeratoPillay is part of a sophisticated network of twitter accounts amplifying the #putsouthafricansfirst hashtag.

Stuart talks about first wave

Jean Show & Tell

Stuart & Jean speculates on the who’s behind the PSAF movement.

We can’t name them explicitly but we can say generically that “small political parties with a nationalistic manifesto” would be the most likely beneficiaries of the campaign.


V/O: So what sort of impact is the hashtag having on average South Africans? Siphesihle Maphumulo is an avid twitter user.

Siphe gives his thoughts on the hashtag

8. 60” OUTRO V/O: South Africans looking for a recourse against disinformation can turn to a website called Real411.org. This is a platform that allows the public to submit potential cases of disinformation, as William Bird from Media Monitoring Africa explains

William explains what real411 does

Talk about the most trending disinformation campaigns in SA this year

Come back to William Bird and how the public can report suspected disinformation

Their claims are assessed by a 3 member panel. William explains what happens after something is flagged as “disinformation”


V/O: But ultimately it is up to us as individuals to always be on the alert for disinformation.

Siphe Closing Comment


PROMOS TEASER:: We get to the truth about the “Put South Africans first” campaign. An innocuous hashtag or dangerous disinformation being used to weaponize xenophobic sentiment among ordinary South Africans.

PROMO 1: As digital media becomes the world’s primary source of news and information, we investigate the risks for South Africans that are becoming ever more vulnerable to digital propaganda and disinformation.

PROMO 2: What is the problem with digital disinformation? We investigate how South Africans are being manipulated through targeted, deliberate digital propaganda and disinformation campaigns.

PROMO 3: We investigate the dissemination of Afrophobic and xenophobic sentiment through fake online social media accounts. Who is weaponizing hashtags, hoping to spread hatred and violence?
